title: TESS light curves (2018-2026) of 630 hot Jupiters show no transiting co-orbital body at L4 or L5: fewer than 2% of hot Jupiters have a coplanar Trojan larger than 2 Earth radii
abstract: Question: Do hot Jupiters have co-orbital (Trojan) companions at L4 or L5 that transit their star? No exotrojan is confirmed, and no published study has stacked TESS photometry at L4/L5 for a large hot-Jupiter sample. Method: We used the 648 hosts and light-curve manifest of a campaign companion search (sci:104e34b6) and analysed 3,780 TESS PDCSAP light curves (sectors 1-107, 2018-2026). For each host we measured a box dip at orbital phases 1/6 (L5) and 5/6 (L4) with the duration of a small body on the planet's chord. We removed the orbital phase curve before a short running-median filter, set the noise from 100 wrong-period folds per host, scanned +-15 degrees for librating bodies, and injected Trojan transits into every light curve (median depth recovery 94%). Results: No point in 630 usable hosts reaches z = 4. The 1,260 z values have a scatter of 0.98; two exceed 3 (1.7 expected). The highest (WASP-54 b, L4, z = 3.7) comes from one sector only. Six libration scans reach p = 0.0099 (6.3 expected). The stacked transiting cross-section per Lagrange point is 0.033 +- 0.027 Earth radii^2 (95% limit 0.078, one 1,800 km body). The median 3-sigma limit on one Trojan is 2.9 Earth radii (21% of the planet radius); 154 hosts are below 2 and 9 below 1 Earth radius. The 95% upper limit on the fraction of hot Jupiters with one coplanar transiting Trojan is 5.2% at 1.5, 2.0% at 2 and 0.9% at 3 Earth radii. Limitations: The test applies only to coplanar Trojans within 15 degrees of the Lagrange points; inclined bodies and broad dust clouds are not tested. Phase-coherent systematics affect a few hosts with large phase curves or long transits (KELT-9 b excluded; TOI-2337 b shows an unphysical brightening). Box shape and generic limb darkening are simplifications.

display.caption: Weighted stack of the TESS box-dip area (Earth radii^2) against orbital phase for 630 hot Jupiters. The profile is flat at L5 (phase 1/6) and L4 (phase 5/6): 0.033 +- 0.027 Earth radii^2 per point.
95% upper limit on the fraction of hot Jupiters with one coplanar transiting Trojan at L4 or L5 against Trojan radius, from zero detections above z = 4 in 630 hosts.
Per-host 3-sigma limits on the radius of one Trojan (worse of L4 and L5) against TESS magnitude, and relative to the hot-Jupiter radius.
